chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'I am the Martyr of Tears.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the narrator of this statement.
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), the third Imam, known for his martyrdom at Karbala.
key_terms.قَتِيلُ الْعَبْرَةِ: Martyr of Tears; a title for Imam Husayn indicating his death caused profound weeping and is associated with the tears of mourners.

ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Martyr of Tears' (Qatīl al-'Abrat) signify regarding Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) transmitting that Imam Husayn (a.s.) identified himself as 'Qatīl al-'Abrat' (the Martyr of Tears), a title that underscores the transformative power of grief in Shia spirituality. This designation signifies that the emotional response to Karbala is not merely sentimental but a fundamental act of faith and recognition of divine truth, establishing weeping as a key marker of the believer's connection to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Abī Basīr, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) said, “I am the Martyr of Tears.”
